purpose: Law-1 visible parked channel. Anything this dedup pass would otherwise have dropped for low confidence or below-threshold quality is routed here rather than deleted. Culling happens at triage (/ledger), never by withholding a finding from the run the human reviews.
zeroParkDeclaration: No candidate was parked, because no candidate was dropped. All six (F-01..F-06) are retained in deduplicated-findings.json; 0 merged away, 0 dropped as a ledger duplicate, 0 filtered as noise. cededDimensions.reason: This is L-07's entire core claim, restated. A genuine duplicate.

Already present verbatim inside L-07's open recommendation: 'parse `.blockNumber` and assert freshness (which also addresses PR-11)'. F-06 claimed staleness as an uncovered increment; source of record says otherwise.

scopeNarrowings.whyThisIsNotASilentDrop: The ceded dimensions are not lost: they sit inside an OPEN ledger entry whose recommendation already names them, and the cession is recorded here, in deduplicated-findings.json, and as a cross-reference the report-writer is instructed to print in F-06's own write-up. L-07 is marked `abandoned` or otherwise disposed of without a fix → re-file BOTH ceded dimensions.

noiseThresholdEvaluations.severity: low (auditor input; not set by this pass)
noiseThresholdEvaluations.consideredFor: QA / tool-noise filter — part 1 is a function-naming defect, and the whole finding is graded LATENT ONLY with a verified-clean current call graph.
noiseThresholdEvaluations.outcome: RETAINED — not parked, not dropped, not downgraded.
noiseThresholdEvaluations.reason: Two grounds. (1) The naming half is not cosmetic: `_requireNoBroadcastFlag` asserts an invariant it structurally cannot check, and this project's standing position (memory: 'in-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority — falsely-exhaustive docs RAISE severity') makes a guard that overstates its own coverage reportable rather than a style nit. (2) The guard-test half is a defence-in-depth defect on the read-only guarantee of a contract protecting a one-shot mainnet cutover, and it is not a finding any automated tool surfaces — 'this test scans for cheatcode string literals and would therefore pass a call to an inherited mutating helper such as _writeProgressFileWithStatus' requires reading the test against the inheritance chain. Latency bounds the SEVERITY, which is the classifier's call; it does not make the finding noise, which is this pass's call.

noiseThresholdEvaluations.consideredFor: low-plausibility filter — the auditor wrote 'Plausibility is low: it requires digit-editing the value, not the trimming slip the runbook warns about. Filed for recall, not because it is likely.'
noiseThresholdEvaluations.reason: Honest self-grading of plausibility is a reason to make a finding LEGIBLE to triage, never a reason to withhold it from the run the human reviews (Law 1: recall beats report-tidiness; confidence is not severity). The guarded asset is the largest single item in the cutover, the recommended fix is cheap (one sibling key plus two requires), and the operator action that triggers it — hand-editing a progress file — is a step the runbook mandates on every resume leg, so the hand is already in the file. Triage may reasonably decide to carry this risk; that decision belongs at /ledger.

noiseThresholdEvaluations.consideredFor: documentation-only filter — the finding explicitly states 'The CODE is unaffected ... The defect is confined to the manual control.'
noiseThresholdEvaluations.reason: The 'documentation/style' carve-out covers NatSpec, formatting and pragmas — not a compensating control that a Medium-severity finding's own risk assessment leans on. The degraded artefact IS the control here. It also meets the Law-3 footgun test squarely: a competent, non-malicious operator would be surprised to find every quoted figure mismatching, and the surprise pushes in a dangerous direction (learning that checklist numbers are 'always a bit off' and waving through a genuine BPT shortfall). Footguns are in scope.

collapsesRefused.proposedBy: script-auditor, in F-06's own description ('should be collapsed into it by the deduplicator')
collapsesRefused.shortReason: Address-set mismatch is a different root cause from file absence. Different failure timing (fail-late inside Phase 6 at :1553, after Phases 1-5 dispatched, leaving a partially-applied one-shot mainnet cutover — versus L-07's own recorded impact of 'atomic, before a single transaction is broadcast'), different blast radius, different mitigation, and a second affected artefact (scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js resolveAddress). Collapsing would have let a future L-07 fix close the entry legitimately while the address cross-check silently never shipped.

Same family, different gates. L-03's gate reads the `deploymentStatus` string from JS; F-02 establishes the verifier never reads `deploymentStatus` at all and gates on record PRESENCE instead. The two gates share no input, and neither accepted fix touches the other.

Same family (blocking probe reachable only on the preview path), opposite sequence positions. L-04 needs its probe moved EARLIER, ahead of the whitelist write; F-01 needs its probe moved LATER, into a post-broadcast read-only leg. No single relocation serves both.

Confirmed distinct, not assumed. Shared artefact (the story-072 checklist) but opposite defect kinds — enforceable-but-unenforced (fails silent) versus stated-but-wrong (fails noisy, then numb) — with non-overlapping fixes in both directions.

Same contract and a shared theme ('the verifier's guards are weaker than their names'), but different invariants (dispatch-completeness vs read-only-ness) and different fixes. Recorded as a systemicTheme for the report-writer to present adjacently, not as a merge.
